# Configuration reference

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/config-docs.ts from packages/core/src/config/schema.ts. Do not edit; run `pnpm docs:config`. -->

Every ReelForge Studio setting, generated from the one configuration schema.
Precedence, lowest to highest (D-029):

1. **default** (below)
2. **file**: the YAML or JSON file named by `RENDERWELD_CONFIG` (old name `REELFORGE_CONFIG`), nested by key
   (`limits.rateLimitPerMinute` is `limits: { rateLimitPerMinute: 120 }`); unknown keys are refused
3. **env**: the environment variables below; the `RENDERWELD_` name wins over older aliases;
   every secret can also be read from a file named by `<NAME>_FILE` (Docker/Kubernetes secrets)

**Renamed from ReelForge** ([RENAMED.md](RENAMED.md)): every `RENDERWELD_*` variable below also works under its old
name `REELFORGE_*` (and `REELFORGE_*_FILE`). The old name alone logs one warning at start naming the new one; both
names set to different values stop the server with an error naming both; both set to the same value is fine.
The old names keep working until a removal date announced in the release notes, at least 90 days after the rename ships.
4. **runtime**: values set over the API (`PATCH /v1/config`, MCP `update_config`, admin scope), stored in the
   database; only settings with scope **runtime**. `null` clears a runtime value.

**Release images** (the published Docker image, D-039) fix `licence.mode` (`required`), `licence.serverUrl` and
`licence.orgId` at build time: their source is **build**, and a config file, environment variable or
`update_config` that tries to change them is refused (`build_locked_setting`). Builds from source (`pnpm dev`,
`--build-arg REELFORGE_EDITION=dev`) keep every setting configurable; `licence.mode: off` there is for
noncommercial development only (LICENSING.md).

Scope **startup** settings are read once at start; changing them at runtime is refused with an error that says
where to set them. `GET /v1/config` / MCP `get_config` show each effective value and its source; secrets show
only `set` / `not set`. Secrets set at runtime are stored encrypted (AES-256-GCM) with `REELFORGE_SECRET_KEY`;
without it the server refuses to store them. Check a configuration without starting the server:
`renderweld config check [--file PATH]`; print the effective one: `renderweld config show` (both name the variable that
supplied each value; `reelforge` is the old name of the command).

Example `renderweld.yaml` (any file name works; `reelforge.yaml` too):

```yaml
server:
  publicUrl: https://studio.example.com
limits:
  rateLimitPerMinute: 120
  renderConcurrency: 2
logging:
  level: info
```

## server

| Key | Env | Type | Default | Scope | Secret | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `server.host` | `RENDERWELD_HOST`; old name `REELFORGE_HOST` | string | `127.0.0.1` | startup |  | Bind address. Keep loopback unless a TLS proxy is in front (`0.0.0.0` in the Docker image). |
| `server.port` | `RENDERWELD_PORT`; old name `REELFORGE_PORT` | integer | `4321` | startup |  | TCP port (`0` picks a free one). |
| `server.publicUrl` | `RENDERWELD_PUBLIC_URL`; old name `REELFORGE_PUBLIC_URL` | url | (none) | startup |  | Public base URL: used in output links and allowed as Host on `/mcp`. Example: `https://studio.example.com`. |
| `server.allowedHosts` | `RENDERWELD_ALLOWED_HOSTS`; old name `REELFORGE_ALLOWED_HOSTS` | list (comma-separated in env) | (empty) | runtime |  | Extra host names accepted on `/mcp` (DNS-rebinding protection), besides localhost and the public URL host. Comma-separated in the environment. Example: `reelforge,studio.internal`. |
| `server.trustProxy` | `RENDERWELD_TRUST_PROXY`; old name `REELFORGE_TRUST_PROXY` | boolean | `false` | runtime |  | Take the client address from the last entry of `X-Forwarded-For` (set by your reverse proxy) instead of the TCP peer, for the audit log and per-key IP allowlists. Only turn it on behind a proxy that sets that header. |
| `server.role` | `RENDERWELD_ROLE`; old name `REELFORGE_ROLE` | `all` \| `api` \| `worker` | `all` | startup |  | What this instance does (D-076). `all`: serve REST/MCP and render (one instance). `api`: serve REST/MCP and enqueue jobs, never render. `worker`: claim and render jobs from the database queue; serves only `/healthz`, `/readyz` and `/metrics`. `api` and `worker` need PostgreSQL or MySQL and remote storage (or `storage.localShared`); see docs/providers/queue-and-scaling.md. |
| `server.workerConcurrency` | `RENDERWELD_WORKER_CONCURRENCY`; old name `REELFORGE_WORKER_CONCURRENCY` | integer | `limits.renderConcurrency` | startup |  | Jobs one `worker` (or `all`) instance claims and renders at the same time. Unset: `limits.renderConcurrency` (which can then be changed at runtime). Scale out with more worker instances rather than a high value here. |
| `server.workerOnce` | `RENDERWELD_WORKER_ONCE`; old name `REELFORGE_WORKER_ONCE` | boolean | `false` | startup |  | Run as `reelforge worker --once` (D-100): claim at most one job, render it and exit (0 succeeded, cancelled or nothing queued; 1 failed; 75 handed back, lease lost, or the `--job` still queued; see docs/providers/backends.md). For job platforms that start one container per unit (KEDA ScaledJob, Azure Container Apps event jobs, AWS Batch, Cloud Run Jobs, ECS RunTask). Implies `server.role` `worker` (same database and storage rules); serves no HTTP. |

## dashboard

| Key | Env | Type | Default | Scope | Secret | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dashboard.enabled` | `RENDERWELD_DASHBOARD_ENABLED`; old name `REELFORGE_DASHBOARD_ENABLED` | boolean | `false` | runtime |  | Serve the web dashboard at `/dashboard` (D-115; docs/public/install/dashboard.md): live jobs with cancel and retry, and the library of projects and renders. Off: `/dashboard` answers 404. It is a client of the public REST API: people sign in with an API key, and every call is checked against that key's scopes. Same Host check as `/mcp` (`server.publicUrl`, `server.allowedHosts`), a strict Content-Security-Policy, no cookies and no external hosts. Not served by `worker` instances. |

## queue

| Key | Env | Type | Default | Scope | Secret | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `queue.driver` | `RENDERWELD_QUEUE_DRIVER`; old name `REELFORGE_QUEUE_DRIVER` | `auto` \| `inprocess` \| `database` | `auto` | startup |  | Job queue (D-075). `inprocess`: the instance runs the jobs it accepted (one instance; jobs interrupted by a restart are marked failed). `database`: jobs are claimed from the database with leases (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` on PostgreSQL/MySQL, an atomic update on SQLite), so several workers share them and a crashed worker's job is retried. `auto`: `database` for the `api` and `worker` roles, else `inprocess`. |
| `queue.leaseSeconds` | `RENDERWELD_QUEUE_LEASE_SECONDS`; old name `REELFORGE_QUEUE_LEASE_SECONDS` | integer | `60` | startup |  | Database queue: how long a claimed job belongs to its worker without a heartbeat. Workers renew the lease every quarter of this; a job whose lease ran out (the worker crashed or lost the database) is queued again, or failed after `queue.maxAttempts`. |
| `queue.maxAttempts` | `RENDERWELD_QUEUE_MAX_ATTEMPTS`; old name `REELFORGE_QUEUE_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | integer | `3` | startup |  | Database queue: claims per job. A job whose lease expired this many times is failed with `lease_expired` instead of being queued again. |
| `queue.pollIntervalMs` | `RENDERWELD_QUEUE_POLL_INTERVAL_MS`; old name `REELFORGE_QUEUE_POLL_INTERVAL_MS` | integer | `1000` | startup |  | Database queue: how often an idle worker looks for queued jobs, and how often `get_job waitSeconds` re-reads a job running on another instance. Empty polls back off up to `queue.pollMaxIntervalMs`; on database errors the interval backs off exponentially up to 30 s. |
| `queue.pollMaxIntervalMs` | `RENDERWELD_QUEUE_POLL_MAX_INTERVAL_MS`; old name `REELFORGE_QUEUE_POLL_MAX_INTERVAL_MS` | integer | `5000` | startup |  | Database queue, `queue.dispatch` `poll` (D-105): after each poll that finds nothing, an idle worker waits twice as long as the last time, from `queue.pollIntervalMs` up to this; a poll that claims a job goes back to `queue.pollIntervalMs`, so a busy queue is polled as before. It bounds the extra queue wait after an idle period (a job enqueued then waits at most this long for a worker with a free slot) and cuts idle database load. Set it to `queue.pollIntervalMs` for no backoff. Also the poll while a `notify` listener is disconnected. |
| `queue.dispatch` | `RENDERWELD_QUEUE_DISPATCH`; old name `REELFORGE_QUEUE_DISPATCH` | `poll` \| `notify` \| `sqs` \| `redis` | `poll` | startup |  | How workers of the database queue learn that a job is ready (D-105; the database stays the queue of record either way). `poll`: idle workers look every `queue.pollIntervalMs`, backing off to `queue.pollMaxIntervalMs`. `notify` (PostgreSQL only): the transaction that queues a job sends `NOTIFY` and workers `LISTEN` on one direct session connection each, so idle workers stop polling and are woken within milliseconds; a fallback poll every `queue.dispatchFallbackSeconds` claims anything a lost message did not announce. `LISTEN` does not work through PgBouncer in transaction or statement mode: set `database.directUrl` then (a worker checks delivery at start and refuses to start without it). Refused at start on MySQL and SQLite. `sqs` (Amazon SQS standard queue, `queue.sqs.*`) and `redis` (Redis Streams with a consumer group, `queue.redis.*`), on every database: the transaction that queues a job writes an outbox row, each instance's relay publishes the job id, one worker receives it, wakes its normal fair claim and acknowledges the message after that claim; idle workers wait on the broker instead of the database, and the broker's queue depth can drive an autoscaler. A broker that is down never blocks an enqueue (the outbox keeps the row and retries) and workers poll until it answers. Set the same value on every instance. NATS JetStream is planned (docs/providers/queue-and-scaling.md). |
| `queue.dispatchFallbackSeconds` | `RENDERWELD_QUEUE_DISPATCH_FALLBACK_SECONDS`; old name `REELFORGE_QUEUE_DISPATCH_FALLBACK_SECONDS` | integer | `30` | startup |  | `queue.dispatch` `notify`, `sqs`, `redis`: how often an idle worker still polls while its listener is connected, so a job whose message was lost (a dropped connection, a job queued by a process without the dispatch setting) waits at most this long. Lower values cost one claim transaction per idle worker per interval. With `sqs` and `redis` also how often each instance's outbox relay looks for rows it did not publish at once (another instance stopped before publishing). |
| `queue.sqs.queueUrl` | `RENDERWELD_QUEUE_SQS_QUEUE_URL`; old name `REELFORGE_QUEUE_SQS_QUEUE_URL` | url | (none) | startup |  | `queue.dispatch` `sqs`: the URL of an SQS **standard** queue (not FIFO) that only this deployment uses. Required with `sqs`. The api and workers need `sqs:SendMessage`; workers also `sqs:ReceiveMessage`, `sqs:DeleteMessage`, `sqs:ChangeMessageVisibility` and `sqs:GetQueueAttributes`. Example: `https://sqs.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/123456789012/reelforge-jobs`. |
| `queue.sqs.region` | `RENDERWELD_QUEUE_SQS_REGION`; old name `REELFORGE_QUEUE_SQS_REGION` | string | the region in `queue.sqs.queueUrl`, else the AWS default (`AWS_REGION`) | startup |  | `queue.dispatch` `sqs`: AWS region of the queue. Example: `eu-west-1`. |
| `queue.sqs.endpoint` | `RENDERWELD_QUEUE_SQS_ENDPOINT`; old name `REELFORGE_QUEUE_SQS_ENDPOINT` | url | (none) | startup |  | `queue.dispatch` `sqs`: SQS API endpoint override (a VPC endpoint, or LocalStack in tests). Empty: the regional AWS endpoint. |
| `queue.sqs.accessKeyId` | `RENDERWELD_QUEUE_SQS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`; old name `REELFORGE_QUEUE_SQS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` (each also as `_FILE`) | string | (none) | runtime | yes | `queue.dispatch` `sqs`: access key id. Leave unset to use the ambient AWS identity (IAM role, IRSA / web identity, `AWS_*` variables). A change at runtime applies to the next SQS call. |
| `queue.sqs.secretAccessKey` | `RENDERWELD_QUEUE_SQS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`; old name `REELFORGE_QUEUE_SQS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` (each also as `_FILE`) | string | (none) | runtime | yes | `queue.dispatch` `sqs`: secret access key (with `accessKeyId`). |
| `queue.sqs.sessionToken` | `RENDERWELD_QUEUE_SQS_SESSION_TOKEN`; old name `REELFORGE_QUEUE_SQS_SESSION_TOKEN` (each also as `_FILE`) | string | (none) | runtime | yes | `queue.dispatch` `sqs`: session token for temporary keys (optional). |
| `queue.sqs.visibilityTimeoutSeconds` | `RENDERWELD_QUEUE_SQS_VISIBILITY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`; old name `REELFORGE_QUEUE_SQS_VISIBILITY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | integer | `30` | startup |  | `queue.dispatch` `sqs`: visibility timeout set on every receive. A message received by a worker that stops before deleting it (deleted after the claim it woke) becomes visible to the other workers after this long; its claim is then a no-op. Shorter: a lost message wakes another worker sooner; it must stay longer than a claim takes (milliseconds) plus network hiccups. |
| `queue.redis.url` | `RENDERWELD_QUEUE_REDIS_URL`; old name `REELFORGE_QUEUE_REDIS_URL` (each also as `_FILE`) | string | (none) | startup | yes | `queue.dispatch` `redis`: the Redis server (6.2 or later; Streams, XAUTOCLAIM). `rediss://` connects with TLS. Required with `redis`. Secret because the URL may hold a password (prefer `queue.redis.password`). Example: `rediss://reelforge@redis.internal:6380/0`. |
| `queue.redis.password` | `RENDERWELD_QUEUE_REDIS_PASSWORD`; old name `REELFORGE_QUEUE_REDIS_PASSWORD` (each also as `_FILE`) | string | (none) | runtime | yes | `queue.dispatch` `redis`: password (Redis AUTH; the user name comes from the URL). Overrides a password in `queue.redis.url`. A change at runtime reconnects. |
| `queue.redis.tlsCaFile` | `RENDERWELD_QUEUE_REDIS_TLS_CA_FILE`; old name `REELFORGE_QUEUE_REDIS_TLS_CA_FILE` | path | (none) | startup |  | `queue.dispatch` `redis` with `rediss://`: a PEM file with the CA that signed the server certificate (private CAs). Unset: the system CAs. |
| `queue.redis.stream` | `RENDERWELD_QUEUE_REDIS_STREAM`; old name `REELFORGE_QUEUE_REDIS_STREAM` | string | `reelforge:jobs` | startup |  | `queue.dispatch` `redis`: stream key. Deployments sharing a Redis server need different keys. |
| `queue.redis.group` | `RENDERWELD_QUEUE_REDIS_GROUP`; old name `REELFORGE_QUEUE_REDIS_GROUP` | string | `reelforge-workers` | startup |  | `queue.dispatch` `redis`: consumer group the workers read through (created with the stream if missing). |
| `queue.redis.claimIdleSeconds` | `RENDERWELD_QUEUE_REDIS_CLAIM_IDLE_SECONDS`; old name `REELFORGE_QUEUE_REDIS_CLAIM_IDLE_SECONDS` | integer | `30` | startup |  | `queue.dispatch` `redis`: an entry delivered to a worker that stopped before acknowledging it (acknowledged after the claim it woke) is reclaimed by another worker with XAUTOCLAIM after it was pending this long; its claim is then a no-op. |
| `queue.redis.maxLength` | `RENDERWELD_QUEUE_REDIS_MAX_LENGTH`; old name `REELFORGE_QUEUE_REDIS_MAX_LENGTH` | integer | `100000` | startup |  | `queue.dispatch` `redis`: the stream is trimmed to about this many entries (XADD MAXLEN ~). Entries trimmed before a worker read them are covered by the fallback poll. |
| `queue.notifyJitterMs` | `RENDERWELD_QUEUE_NOTIFY_JITTER_MS`; old name `REELFORGE_QUEUE_NOTIFY_JITTER_MS` | integer | `50` | startup |  | `queue.dispatch` `notify`: a message wakes every idle worker, so each waits a random delay of up to this long before it claims, and skips the claim when other workers already claimed the announced jobs meanwhile (each claim is announced too). Larger: fewer empty claims per job when many workers are idle; smaller: less added queue wait (on average this divided by the number of idle workers, plus one). |
| `queue.shutdownGraceSeconds` | `RENDERWELD_QUEUE_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS`; old name `REELFORGE_QUEUE_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS` | integer | `30` | startup |  | On SIGTERM a worker stops claiming and waits this long for its running jobs; jobs still running then are stopped and handed back to the queue (database queue), so another worker takes them at once. Keep the orchestrator's grace period (Kubernetes `terminationGracePeriodSeconds`) longer. |
| `queue.onceWaitMs` | `RENDERWELD_QUEUE_ONCE_WAIT_MS`; old name `REELFORGE_QUEUE_ONCE_WAIT_MS` | integer | 3 × `queue.pollIntervalMs` | startup |  | `worker --once`: how long to wait for a queued job before exiting 0 with nothing done, so a job platform does not pay for an idle container. `reelforge worker --once --wait-ms N` overrides it. |
| `queue.priorityAgingSeconds` | `RENDERWELD_QUEUE_PRIORITY_AGING_SECONDS`; old name `REELFORGE_QUEUE_PRIORITY_AGING_SECONDS` | integer | `600` | runtime |  | Job priorities (D-103): jobs are claimed `interactive` (previews) first, then `standard` (renders), then `batch`. A `batch` job that has waited this long is claimed as `standard` (never as `interactive`), so a steady stream of renders cannot starve batch work. `0`: strict classes (batch waits while any higher job can be claimed). |

## limits

| Key | Env | Type | Default | Scope | Secret | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limits.rateLimitPerMinute` | `RENDERWELD_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE`; old name `REELFORGE_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` | integer | `300` | runtime |  | Requests per minute per API key (`0` disables the limit). |
| `limits.rateLimitStore` | `RENDERWELD_RATE_LIMIT_STORE`; old name `REELFORGE_RATE_LIMIT_STORE` | `auto` \| `memory` \| `database` | `auto` | startup |  | Where per-key request counts live (D-078). `memory`: a token bucket per instance (with several API instances each allows the full limit). `database`: a sliding 60-second window from one counter per key and minute in the database, shared by every instance. `auto`: `database` when the job queue is `database`, else `memory`. |
| `limits.preAuthPerMinute` | `RENDERWELD_PRE_AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE`; old name `REELFORGE_PRE_AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` | integer | `1200` | runtime |  | Requests per minute per client address (`server.trustProxy` decides which one; IPv6 per /64), checked before the API key is looked up, so a flood costs no database work. Per instance, in memory. Several keys behind one address share it, so keep it above `limits.rateLimitPerMinute`. `0` disables it. |
| `limits.authFailuresPerMinute` | `RENDERWELD_AUTH_FAILURES_PER_MINUTE`; old name `REELFORGE_AUTH_FAILURES_PER_MINUTE` | integer | `20` | runtime |  | Failed authentications (missing, unknown, revoked or expired key) per minute per client address; the one that uses them up locks the address out (`limits.authLockoutSeconds`). While locked out, its requests get `429` without a key lookup. Per instance, in memory. `0` disables the lockout. |
| `limits.authLockoutSeconds` | `RENDERWELD_AUTH_LOCKOUT_SECONDS`; old name `REELFORGE_AUTH_LOCKOUT_SECONDS` | integer | `60` | runtime |  | The first lockout after too many failed authentications; each further lockout of the same address doubles, up to `limits.authLockoutMaxSeconds`. |
| `limits.authLockoutMaxSeconds` | `RENDERWELD_AUTH_LOCKOUT_MAX_SECONDS`; old name `REELFORGE_AUTH_LOCKOUT_MAX_SECONDS` | integer | `3600` | runtime |  | The longest lockout. An address with no failed authentication for this long starts over at `limits.authLockoutSeconds`. |
| `limits.maxUploadBytes` | `RENDERWELD_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES`; old name `REELFORGE_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` | integer | `209715200` | runtime |  | Largest asset upload or URL import, in bytes. Uploads and imports are streamed to a temporary file and stopped as soon as they pass it (`413 too_large`); they are never held in memory whole. |
| `limits.maxJsonBytes` | `RENDERWELD_MAX_JSON_BYTES`; old name `REELFORGE_MAX_JSON_BYTES` | integer | `2097152` | runtime |  | Largest JSON request body, in bytes. |
| `limits.renderConcurrency` | `RENDERWELD_RENDER_CONCURRENCY`; old name `REELFORGE_RENDER_CONCURRENCY` | integer | `1` | runtime |  | Renders at the same time. Measured best: the number of vCPUs; memory about 0.3 GB plus 0.6 GB per render for 1080x1920 (docs/public/install/sizing.md, `pnpm bench:docker`). More than the vCPUs only slows each render: on 1 vCPU two at once finished fewer an hour than one. A lower value lets running renders finish. |
| `limits.maxInflightRequests` | `RENDERWELD_MAX_INFLIGHT_REQUESTS`; old name `REELFORGE_MAX_INFLIGHT_REQUESTS` | integer | `64` | runtime |  | Requests one instance works on at the same time (0 = no limit). One more waits up to `limits.inflightWaitMs` for a slot, then is answered with `503 overloaded` and `Retry-After: 1`, instead of queueing behind the database pool until a timeout or a 500 (D-117, docs/SCALE.md). Not counted: `/healthz`, `/readyz`, `/metrics`, long-polls (`?wait=`) and event streams, which hold no database connection while they wait. Keep it a small multiple of the database pool (`connection_limit`, 10 for an api instance): more requests in progress than the pool serves only wait inside it. |
| `limits.inflightWaitMs` | `RENDERWELD_INFLIGHT_WAIT_MS`; old name `REELFORGE_INFLIGHT_WAIT_MS` | integer | `3000` | runtime |  | How long a request over `limits.maxInflightRequests` waits for a slot, first come first served, before `503 overloaded` (milliseconds; 0 = refuse at once). Absorbs short bursts; keep it below your clients' timeouts. |
| `limits.maxQueuedJobsPerKey` | `RENDERWELD_MAX_QUEUED_JOBS_PER_KEY`; old name `REELFORGE_MAX_QUEUED_JOBS_PER_KEY` | integer | `100` | runtime |  | Unfinished render and preview jobs (queued or running) one API key may have. Another start is refused with `429 too_many_jobs` and `Retry-After` until one finishes. Counted in the database, so it holds across instances. Raise it (or `0`) for one organisation key that feeds a large worker fleet. `0`: no limit. |
| `limits.maxQueuedJobs` | `RENDERWELD_MAX_QUEUED_JOBS`; old name `REELFORGE_MAX_QUEUED_JOBS` | integer | `1000` with the in-process queue, `0` (no limit) with the database queue | runtime |  | Render and preview jobs that may wait in the queue in total (every key, every instance). A start beyond it is refused with `429 queue_full` and `Retry-After`. The default follows the effective queue (`queue.driver`, `server.role`): a single instance keeps its queue bounded, the database queue is unbounded because the database and autoscaled workers absorb the load. `0`: no limit. With the database queue, a value here makes every start in the deployment wait for one shared row lock (held for two database round trips per start), which caps the total start rate; prefer `maxQueuedJobsPerKey` there unless the queue itself must be bounded. |
| `limits.maxRunningJobsPerKey` | `RENDERWELD_MAX_RUNNING_JOBS_PER_KEY`; old name `REELFORGE_MAX_RUNNING_JOBS_PER_KEY` | integer | `0` | runtime |  | Jobs of one API key that run at the same time; that key's other jobs wait while other keys' jobs run. Off by default: jobs are always claimed fairly across keys (the key with the fewest running jobs first), so one key cannot starve others, and a single organisation key can still use every worker. Set it to reserve capacity. With several workers claiming at the same moment a key may briefly get one more. `0`: no limit. |
| `limits.maxEstimatedWaitSeconds` | `RENDERWELD_MAX_ESTIMATED_WAIT_SECONDS`; old name `REELFORGE_MAX_ESTIMATED_WAIT_SECONDS` | integer | `0` | runtime |  | Admission control (D-103): refuse a new render or preview with `429 queue_full`, `Retry-After` and `details` (queued jobs ahead, estimated wait) when its estimated queue wait is longer than this. The estimate is measured, not configured: the smaller of how long the oldest queued job of the same or a higher priority has waited and the jobs ahead divided by the claim throughput of the last minutes (shared by every instance through the database). Checked in the same statement as the job caps. `0`: off. |
| `limits.maxRenderSeconds` | `RENDERWELD_MAX_RENDER_SECONDS`; old name `REELFORGE_MAX_RENDER_SECONDS` | integer | `180` | runtime |  | Longest render or preview, in seconds. Longer projects are refused with `422 render_limit_exceeded`. Up to 14400 (4 hours, the most a manifest describes); long renders need disk for every clip and time per frame, so raise `maxRenderFrames` with it and consider `render.fanOut` (docs/CONFIG.md, #302). |
| `limits.maxRenderFrames` | `RENDERWELD_MAX_RENDER_FRAMES`; old name `REELFORGE_MAX_RENDER_FRAMES` | integer | `5400` | runtime |  | Most frames in one render or preview (duration × fps; 5400 is 180 s at 30 fps or 90 s at 60 fps; at most 864000, 4 hours at 60 fps). Refused with `422 render_limit_exceeded`. |
| `limits.maxScenes` | `RENDERWELD_MAX_SCENES`; old name `REELFORGE_MAX_SCENES` | integer | `50` | runtime |  | Most scenes in one render (up to 2000, the most a manifest holds). Refused with `422 render_limit_exceeded`. |
| `limits.maxRenderDimension` | `RENDERWELD_MAX_RENDER_DIMENSION`; old name `REELFORGE_MAX_RENDER_DIMENSION` | integer | `3840` | runtime |  | Largest output width or height in pixels (3840 allows 4K in either orientation; the schema allows 4096). Refused with `422 render_limit_exceeded`. |
| `limits.maxRenderFps` | `RENDERWELD_MAX_RENDER_FPS`; old name `REELFORGE_MAX_RENDER_FPS` | integer | `60` | runtime |  | Highest output frame rate (supported: 23.976, 24, 25, 29.97, 30, 48, 50, 59.94, 60). Refused with `422 render_limit_exceeded`. |
| `limits.providerRunsPerKeyPerDay` | `RENDERWELD_PROVIDER_RUNS_PER_KEY_PER_DAY`; old name `REELFORGE_PROVIDER_RUNS_PER_KEY_PER_DAY` | integer | `500` | runtime |  | Provider calls (`run_provider`, `generate_voice`) one API key may make per UTC day; cached results do not count, failed calls do. | `database.readUrl` | `RENDERWELD_DATABASE_READ_URL`, `DATABASE_READ_URL`; old name `REELFORGE_DATABASE_READ_URL` (each also as `_FILE`) | string | (none) | startup | yes | A read replica of `database.url` (PostgreSQL or MySQL; refused with SQLite) for the list reads that tolerate lag: list_projects, list_project_versions, list_jobs, list_assets, list_themes, list_audit_events and audit exports. Job state, claims, quotas, rate limits, keys, licence, idempotency and every read-then-write stay on `database.url`. Unset: everything uses `database.url`. Never migrated. See docs/providers/queue-and-scaling.md#read-replica. Example: `postgresql://reelforge:<password>@db-replica:5432/reelforge`. |
| `database.workerConnectionLimit` | `RENDERWELD_DB_WORKER_CONNECTION_LIMIT`; old name `REELFORGE_DB_WORKER_CONNECTION_LIMIT` | integer | `3` | startup |  | Pool size of a `worker` role process when its database URL has no `?connection_limit=` (claims, heartbeats and progress need few connections; hundreds of workers at the drivers' default of 10 each would exhaust the database). `0`: the driver default (10). Other roles keep the driver default. Sizing: docs/providers/queue-and-scaling.md#connection-pooling. |
| `database.directUrl` | `RENDERWELD_DATABASE_DIRECT_URL`, `DATABASE_DIRECT_URL`; old name `REELFORGE_DATABASE_DIRECT_URL` (each also as `_FILE`) | string | `database.url` | startup | yes | A direct session connection to the PostgreSQL server, for what a transaction-mode pooler cannot carry. Today: the `LISTEN` connection of `queue.dispatch` `notify` (one per worker). Required when `database.url` goes through PgBouncer in transaction or statement mode (or a similar pooler); the queries keep using `database.url`. Unset: `database.url`. Secret because the URL usually holds a password. Example: `postgresql://reelforge:<password>@db:5432/reelforge`. |
| `database.migrateOnStart` | `RENDERWELD_MIGRATE_ON_START`; old name `REELFORGE_MIGRATE_ON_START` | boolean | `true` | startup |  | Apply pending migrations on start. Off: refuse to start while migrations are pending (run `renderweld migrate`). |

## security

| Key | Env | Type | Default | Scope | Secret | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `security.secretKey` | `RENDERWELD_SECRET_KEY`; old name `REELFORGE_SECRET_KEY` (each also as `_FILE`) | string | (none) | startup | yes | Encrypts secrets stored in the database (provider keys, licence key) with AES-256-GCM and keys the integrity seal of the stored licence state. At least 32 characters: `openssl rand -base64 32`. **Required by the release edition**: it does not start without it (#305). A dev build without it refuses to store secrets and seals the licence state with a random key in `<dataDir>/licence-seal.key` (instances sharing a database then need the same secret key). Keep it safe: losing it makes stored secrets unreadable. |
| `security.bootstrapKey` | `RENDERWELD_BOOTSTRAP_KEY`; old name `REELFORGE_BOOTSTRAP_KEY` (each also as `_FILE`) | string | (none) | startup | yes | First admin API key: `rf_` + at least 32 random URL-safe characters (`rf_$(openssl rand -hex 24)`); low-entropy values are refused. Stored hashed as key "bootstrap" on start if no key exists. |
| `security.oauth.issuer` | `RENDERWELD_MCP_OAUTH_ISSUER`; old name `REELFORGE_MCP_OAUTH_ISSUER` | url | (none) | startup |  | Turns on OAuth for `/mcp`: the issuer identifier of your authorization server, exactly as in its tokens' `iss` (trailing slash included). `/mcp` then also accepts its JWT access tokens (asymmetric signatures, keys from its JWKS) with `reelforge:read`, `reelforge:write`, `reelforge:render`, `reelforge:admin` or `reelforge:owner` (instance settings, workspaces) in `scope`/`scp`, and serves `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`. API keys keep working. Unset: API keys only. Example: `https://auth.example.com/realms/studio`. |
| `security.oauth.audience` | `RENDERWELD_MCP_OAUTH_AUDIENCE`; old name `REELFORGE_MCP_OAUTH_AUDIENCE` | url | (none) | startup |  | What a token's `aud` must contain: this server's MCP URL (RFC 8707 resource indicator). Default: `server.publicUrl` + `/mcp` (one of them is required with an issuer). Example: `https://studio.example.com/mcp`. |
| `security.oauth.jwksUrl` | `RENDERWELD_MCP_OAUTH_JWKS_URL`; old name `REELFORGE_MCP_OAUTH_JWKS_URL` | url | (none) | startup |  | The issuer's JWKS. Default: `jwks_uri` from its metadata (`/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`, then OpenID discovery). |

| Key | Env | Type | Default | Scope | Secret | Description |

| `render.chromiumPath` | `RENDERWELD_CHROMIUM_PATH`; old name `REELFORGE_CHROMIUM_PATH` | path | (none; set in Docker) | startup |  | Chrome Headless Shell binary used by every engine. |

The sandbox is on by default everywhere, the release image included (run it with `deployment/seccomp/chrome.json`, docs/security/HARDENING.md). `true` is an explicit opt-out: it is logged at start and reported in `get_capabilities` and `/readyz`. |
| `render.sceneTimeoutSeconds` | `RENDERWELD_RENDER_SCENE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`; old name `REELFORGE_RENDER_SCENE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | integer | `900` | startup |  | Hard limit for rendering one html or hyperframes scene, whatever its length (engines use their per-frame estimate when it is shorter). 30 to 3600 seconds. |
| `render.timeoutSeconds` | `RENDERWELD_RENDER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`; old name `REELFORGE_RENDER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | integer | `3600` | runtime |  | Longest time one render or preview job (or one unit or join of a fanned-out render) may run on a worker; then it is stopped and fails with `render_timeout` (the `render.timeout` event). `0`: no limit. Read when the job starts. |
| `render.encoderThreads` | `RENDERWELD_RENDER_ENCODER_THREADS`; old name `REELFORGE_RENDER_ENCODER_THREADS` | integer | `2` | runtime |  | Threads of each H.264 encode (x264), and of the decoders and filters in the same FFmpeg process (0 to 64). `0`: x264's own choice, 1.5 per CPU core, so memory per render grows with the machine (607 MB for a 1080x1920 encode on 4 vCPU, more on bigger nodes). The default 2 keeps a 1080x1920 encode near 350 MB with the same output (the thread count does not change the encoded video) and still encodes faster than a browser renders frames; a node gets its parallelism from running several renders (`server.workerConcurrency`). Clips of workers with other values still join by stream copy. Measurements: docs/SCALE.md. |
| `render.encoderLookahead` | `RENDERWELD_RENDER_ENCODER_LOOKAHEAD`; old name `REELFORGE_RENDER_ENCODER_LOOKAHEAD` | integer | `20` | runtime |  | Frames x264's rate control looks ahead (`rc-lookahead`, 0 to 250); each one is held in memory at full size. `0`: the preset's own (40 for `medium`). The default 20 halves that buffer for a small, measured quality cost (1080x1920: SSIM 0.99965 instead of 0.99972 against the source frames, files 7 % smaller); docs/SCALE.md. |
| `render.fanOut` | `RENDERWELD_RENDER_FAN_OUT`; old name `REELFORGE_RENDER_FAN_OUT` | `off` \| `scenes` \| `scenes+chunks` | `off` | runtime |  | Split one render across workers (D-097, docs/providers/queue-and-scaling.md#render-fan-out). `off`: one worker renders every scene and assembles the video (the default; unchanged behaviour). `scenes`: with the database queue, a `render` of the `local` backend with two or more scenes becomes one `render_unit` job per scene, claimed by any worker, and one `render_join` job that assembles and commits the video; previews and the in-process queue always use one worker. `scenes+chunks`: as `scenes`, and a scene of at least `render.chunkMinSceneSeconds` whose engine renders frame ranges (Remotion; not html, Motion Canvas or HyperFrames) is split into chunks of `render.chunkSeconds`, one unit each, so one long scene no longer bounds the render's latency. |
| `render.chunkSeconds` | `RENDERWELD_RENDER_CHUNK_SECONDS`; old name `REELFORGE_RENDER_CHUNK_SECONDS` | number | `4` | runtime |  | With `render.fanOut: scenes+chunks`: length of one chunk of a split scene, in seconds of video (1 to 600). The last chunk takes the rest: it is shorter, or up to half a chunk longer when the rest would be under half a chunk. Shorter chunks spread a scene over more workers; each chunk pays a browser start and an encode of its own. |
| `render.chunkMinSceneSeconds` | `RENDERWELD_RENDER_CHUNK_MIN_SCENE_SECONDS`; old name `REELFORGE_RENDER_CHUNK_MIN_SCENE_SECONDS` | number | `8` | runtime |  | With `render.fanOut: scenes+chunks`: scenes shorter than this (seconds, 2 to 3600) are never split and render as one unit. |
| `render.audio.loudness` | `RENDERWELD_RENDER_AUDIO_LOUDNESS`; old name `REELFORGE_RENDER_AUDIO_LOUDNESS` | `social` \| `broadcast-ebu` \| `broadcast-atsc` \| `podcast` \| `off` | `social` | runtime |  | Loudness preset of renders whose manifest sets no `audio.loudness` and whose `render_project` call passes none (#301, docs/public/manifest/audio.md). `social`: -14 LUFS, true peak -2 dBTP; `broadcast-ebu`: EBU R 128, -23 LUFS, -1 dBTP; `broadcast-atsc`: ATSC A/85, -24 LKFS, -2 dBTP; `podcast`: -16 LUFS, -1 dBTP; `off`: the mix as it is. Two-pass FFmpeg loudnorm, measured again after the AAC encode. |

| `render.audio.mutedTrack` | `RENDERWELD_RENDER_AUDIO_MUTED_TRACK`; old name `REELFORGE_RENDER_AUDIO_MUTED_TRACK` | `silent` \| `none` | `silent` | runtime |  | What a muted render (`audio.mute`) carries: `silent`, a valid silent AAC track (safest: some players and upload pipelines expect an audio stream); `none`, no audio stream at all. |
| `render.ffmpegPath` | `RENDERWELD_FFMPEG_PATH`, `FFMPEG_PATH`; old name `REELFORGE_FFMPEG_PATH` | path | `ffmpeg` on PATH | startup |  | FFmpeg binary (system build; 6.1 and 5.1.9 tested). |

Only the key and a random instance id are sent to the licence server (docs/PRIVACY.md). |

| Env | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `RENDERWELD_CONFIG`; old name `REELFORGE_CONFIG` | Path of the config file (YAML or JSON). Both set to different files is an error. |
| `RENDERWELD_IMAGE_DEFAULTS` | Set by the Docker image: its own defaults (`NAME=value`, space-separated), which give way to any value set under either name. |
| `RENDERWELD_LICENCE_KEY_INPUT`; old name `REELFORGE_LICENCE_KEY_INPUT` | The key for `renderweld licence activate` when none is given on the command line. |
| Provider settings declared by plugins | Set with `configure_provider` / `PUT /v1/providers/:id/config` (stored encrypted, like `providers.*`) or the environment variable the provider names. |
| `HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY`, `DO_NOT_TRACK`, `CHECKPOINT_DISABLE` | Telemetry opt-outs for third-party tools, set in the Docker image. |
